name: Cervical cytology (Bethesda 2014)
label: Cervical smear
source: Cytology suite. Classification systems: Bethesda 2023 (thyroid), Milan 2nd ed 2023 (salivary), Paris System 2.0 (urine), International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology (effusions), Sydney System (lymph node), Bethesda 2014 (cervical). Adequacy is assessed on the final preparations only.

options.label: Generate the preparations line (received / processed as)

fields.label: Interpretation (Bethesda 2014)
options: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US)
Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL (ASC-H)
HSIL with features suspicious for invasion
fields.default: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy

reference.title: Bethesda 2014 categories
reference.intro: Criteria from The Bethesda System for Reporting Cervical Cytology (3rd edition, 2014). Nuclear size is judged against a normal intermediate squamous cell nucleus, about 35 µm².

groups.heading: NILM
points: Superficial and intermediate squamous cells; metaplastic cells with dense cyanophilic cytoplasm and regular nuclei
Endocervical cells in honeycomb sheets or palisaded strips; a transformation zone component needs at least 10 well-preserved endocervical or squamous metaplastic cells
Reactive change: nuclei 1.5 to 2 times an intermediate nucleus, smooth outlines, fine chromatin; nucleoli may be prominent

images.caption: Superficial (eosinophilic, polygonal) and intermediate (basophilic) squamous cells in a negative smear (Papanicolaou, x400).
images.credit: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical College, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Endocervical cells in a honeycomb sheet; the mild crowding here may be reactive (Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Squamous metaplastic cells: dense, refractile cyanophilic cytoplasm with projections, moderately enlarged nuclei with regular outlines and fine, even chromatin (annotated, Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: ASC-US
points: Changes suggestive of LSIL, insufficient in degree or extent
Mature (superficial or intermediate) cells; nuclei 2.5 to 3 times an intermediate nucleus; N:C ratio slightly raised
Minimal hyperchromasia and irregularity of chromatin or outline; atypical parakeratosis can qualify

images.caption: ASC-US: a small group of squamous cells with mildly enlarged nuclei and a slightly raised N:C ratio, beside normal superficial and intermediate cells (Pap stain).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: ASC-US: a group of mature squamous cells with orangeophilic cytoplasm and mildly enlarged, slightly hyperchromatic nuclei (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: ASC-H
points: Changes suggestive of HSIL, insufficient for a definitive interpretation
Usually few cells, singly or in small groups, the size of metaplastic cells; nuclei 1.5 to 2.5 times a metaplastic nucleus, high N:C ratio
Patterns: atypical immature metaplasia, crowded sheets, atypical repair and atrophy-like cells; compare with HSIL

images.caption: ASC-H: a single small cell with a hyperchromatic nucleus and a high N:C ratio (Pap stain, x40 objective).
images.credit: Hata et al., Asian Pac J Cancer Prev 2019, Fig 1

images.caption: ASC-H (A) compared with HSIL (B) in liquid-based preparations (x40 objective).
images.credit: Liu et al., J Cancer 2024, Fig 2

images.caption: ASC-H, favour HSIL: a syncytial hyperchromatic crowded group (6A) and isolated small cells with a high N:C ratio (6B), each beside its biopsy (SurePath; H&E).
images.credit: Chivukula and Shidham, CytoJournal 2006, Fig 6

groups.heading: LSIL
points: Mature (superficial or intermediate) cells, singly or in sheets
Nuclei more than 3 times an intermediate nucleus, hyperchromatic, with irregular outlines; bi- and multinucleation are common
Koilocytosis (sharply defined perinuclear cavity, dense rim) is common, but the nuclear changes are what is required

images.caption: LSIL: an enlarged, darker nucleus with coarse chromatin and an irregular contour, beside an unremarkable intermediate cell (annotated, Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Koilocyte: a binucleate squamous cell with a sharply defined perinuclear cavity and a dense peripheral rim of cytoplasm (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: A group of koilocytes with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei, with two normal intermediate cells for comparison (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: HSIL
points: Smaller, less mature cells with lacy, delicate or dense metaplastic cytoplasm, singly, in sheets or in syncytial aggregates
Much higher N:C ratio than LSIL, hyperchromasia, fine or coarsely granular chromatin and irregular nuclear membranes; nucleoli usually absent
Hyperchromatic crowded groups: compare with endocervical cells, atrophy and AIS

images.caption: HSIL: small cells with a high N:C ratio and hyperchromatic, irregular nuclei (right), with intermediate cells for comparison (left) (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: HSIL: isolated small cells with a high N:C ratio and coarse chromatin, beside a superficial cell (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: HSIL (CIN 2-3): a loose group of small cells with a high N:C ratio and hyperchromatic nuclei, beside intermediate cells (SurePath).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: HSIL: a crowded aggregate of cells with high N:C ratios and hyperchromatic nuclei, below intermediate cells (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Squamous cell carcinoma
points: Keratinising: single cells with bizarre (caudate, spindle) shapes, dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and opaque hyperchromatic nuclei; less diathesis
Non-keratinising: syncytial aggregates; coarsely clumped chromatin, prominent nucleoli and a tumour diathesis
HSIL with features suspicious for invasion: a tumour diathesis, macronucleoli or irregular chromatin, short of frank carcinoma

images.caption: Keratinising squamous cell carcinoma: tailed cells with orangeophilic keratinised cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei with granular, irregular chromatin and visible nucleoli, in a dirty background (annotated, Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix: keratinised malignant cells with hyperchromatic nuclei among inflammatory cells and debris (Pap stain, x200).
images.credit: National Cancer Institute, via Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: AGC and its mimics
points: Endocervical: sheets and strips with crowding and overlap, nuclei 3 to 5 times a normal endocervical nucleus, mild hyperchromasia, occasional nucleoli
Endometrial: small groups of cells with slightly enlarged nuclei, mild hyperchromasia, small nucleoli and scant, sometimes vacuolated cytoplasm
Favour neoplastic falls just short of AIS or adenocarcinoma; mimics include tubal metaplasia and lower uterine segment cells

images.caption: Atypical endometrial cells: a tight, degenerate three-dimensional cluster with a high N:C ratio and small faint nucleoli, short of adenocarcinoma in quantity and quality (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 3

images.caption: Tubal metaplasia mimicking AIS, with milder crowding, elongation and stratification; no cilia were found and it was called AGC-NOS, endocervical (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 12

images.caption: Lower uterine segment cells: a tightly packed, uniform honeycomb sheet; without the usual stroma it was called AGC-NOS (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 13

groups.heading: Endocervical AIS
points: Crowded sheets, strips and rosettes; pseudostratification and feathering at the edges
Elongated hyperchromatic nuclei with evenly dispersed, coarsely granular chromatin; nucleoli small or absent
Mitoses and apoptotic bodies; the background is usually clean

images.caption: AIS: a crowded group of columnar cells with elongated, overlapping hyperchromatic nuclei, beside superficial squamous cells (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: AIS: a crowded strip with pseudostratification and a feathered edge; elongated hyperchromatic nuclei without nucleoli. Called AGC, favour neoplastic, on two fragments; AIS on histology (Pap stain, x200).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 11

images.caption: AIS: a three-dimensional group of crowded columnar cells with hyperchromatic nuclei (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Adenocarcinoma
points: Endocervical: abundant cells in sheets, strips and three-dimensional clusters; enlarged pleomorphic nuclei, irregular chromatin with clearing, macronucleoli; tumour diathesis
Endometrial: fewer cells, singly or in small three-dimensional clusters; vacuolated cytoplasm, nucleoli; a finely granular, watery diathesis
Extrauterine: a clean background, papillary groups or psammoma bodies

images.caption: Endocervical adenocarcinoma: a crowded three-dimensional cluster of malignant cells with mucin-filled cytoplasmic vacuoles; a normal intermediate cell lies to the right (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Endocervical adenocarcinoma: mucin streaks with necrotic mucinous cells, like an ileal conduit urine, a background that points to an endocervical primary (Pap stain, x200).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 5

images.caption: Endometrial serous carcinoma on a Pap test: a small cluster of cells with large pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli, beside superficial squamous cells (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Endometrial debris: a watery diathesis with foamy histiocytes, degenerate necrotic debris and phagocytosis, a pattern that points to an endometrial lesion (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 4

fields.label: ASC-US features

is: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US)

fields.help: Bethesda 2014: changes suggestive of LSIL but insufficient in degree or extent. Mature (superficial or intermediate) cells with nuclei 2.5 to 3 times the area of an intermediate nucleus (about 35 µm²) and a slightly raised N:C ratio; minimal hyperchromasia and irregularity of chromatin or outline. Atypical parakeratosis (miniature cells with dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and atypical nuclei) may qualify. Prints as a sentence before the interpretation.

fields.label: ASC-H features

is: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL (ASC-H)

fields.help: Bethesda 2014: changes suggestive of HSIL but insufficient for a definitive interpretation. Usually few cells, singly or in small groups, the size of metaplastic cells, with nuclei 1.5 to 2.5 times a normal metaplastic nucleus and an N:C ratio approaching that of HSIL. Patterns include atypical immature metaplasia, crowded sheets, atypical repair and atrophy-like cells.

fields.label: LSIL features
fields.help: Bethesda 2014: changes in mature (superficial or intermediate) cells, singly or in sheets. Nuclear enlargement more than 3 times an intermediate nucleus, hyperchromasia, uniformly dense or smudged chromatin and irregular outlines; bi- and multinucleation are common. Koilocytosis (a sharply defined perinuclear cavity with a dense peripheral rim) is common but not required; the nuclear changes are.

fields.label: HSIL features

is: HSIL with features suspicious for invasion

fields.help: Bethesda 2014: smaller, less mature cells (lacy, delicate or dense metaplastic cytoplasm, occasionally keratinised), singly, in sheets or in syncytial aggregates. Nuclear enlargement like LSIL but with less cytoplasm, so a much higher N:C ratio; hyperchromasia, fine or coarsely granular chromatin and marked irregularity of the nuclear membrane; nucleoli are generally absent.

fields.label: Features suspicious for invasion

is: HSIL with features suspicious for invasion

fields.help: Bethesda 2014: HSIL with features suspicious for invasion when a tumour diathesis, macronucleoli or irregularly distributed chromatin is present without the features of frank carcinoma. Tick what raised the suspicion; it prints after the HSIL description.

fields.label: Squamous carcinoma features
fields.help: Keratinising: mostly single cells with bizarre (caudate, spindle) shapes, dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and opaque hyperchromatic nuclei; the diathesis may be slight. Non-keratinising: single cells or syncytial aggregates with cyanophilic cytoplasm, coarsely clumped irregular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and a tumour diathesis (granular necrotic debris and old blood).

fields.label: AGC features
fields.help: Bethesda 2014, endocervical: sheets and strips with nuclear crowding and overlap or pseudostratification; nuclei 3 to 5 times the area of normal endocervical nuclei, mild hyperchromasia, occasional nucleoli, rare mitoses; cell borders often discernible. Favour neoplastic falls just short of AIS or adenocarcinoma, in quantity or quality (rosettes, feathering, more crowding). Shown for origin not otherwise specified, endocervical and extrauterine.

fields.label: AGC features (endometrial)
fields.help: Bethesda 2014, endometrial: small groups, usually of 5 to 10 cells; nuclei slightly enlarged compared with normal endometrial cells, mild hyperchromasia, small nucleoli; scant, occasionally vacuolated cytoplasm and ill-defined cell borders.

fields.label: AIS features
fields.help: Bethesda 2014: crowded sheets, strips and rosettes with nuclear pseudostratification and feathering at the edges; enlarged, elongated, hyperchromatic nuclei with evenly dispersed, coarsely granular chromatin; nucleoli small or inconspicuous; mitoses and apoptotic bodies common; the background is usually clean, without a tumour diathesis.

fields.label: Adenocarcinoma features
fields.help: Endocervical: abundant abnormal cells in sheets, strips and three-dimensional clusters; enlarged pleomorphic nuclei, irregular chromatin with parachromatin clearing, macronucleoli and a tumour diathesis. Endometrial: fewer cells, singly or in small three-dimensional clusters, with nucleoli, vacuolated cytoplasm and a finely granular, watery diathesis. Extrauterine: a clean background, papillary groups or psammoma bodies.

fields.label: Organisms and non-neoplastic findings
options: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis
fields.help: Bethesda 2014 organisms and other non-neoplastic findings; each prints as a short description of what was seen. Reporting reactive change is optional. Endometrial cells are reported in women aged 45 or older. Koilocytosis is described under LSIL.

reference.title: Organisms and non-neoplastic findings
reference.intro: Criteria from The Bethesda System (2014). Organisms are reported under NILM; reporting reactive change is optional.

groups.heading: Trichomonas vaginalis
points: Pear-shaped, oval or round cyanophilic organisms, 15 to 30 µm, with a pale, eccentric nucleus and eosinophilic cytoplasmic granules
Flagella are seldom seen; neutrophils, small perinuclear halos and Leptothrix often accompany them

images.caption: Trichomonas vaginalis: pear-shaped and oval cyanophilic organisms with pale, eccentric nuclei among squamous cells (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Trichomonas vaginalis with neutrophils among squamous cells (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Alex_brollo, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Candida
points: Budding yeasts (3 to 7 µm) and pseudohyphae, eosinophilic to grey-brown
Pseudohyphae may spear stacked squamous cells (shish kebab)

images.caption: Candida: a tangle of pseudohyphae and budding yeasts among squamous cells (liquid-based preparation).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Candida: pseudohyphae among squamous cells and neutrophils (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Shift in flora (bacterial vaginosis)
points: Filmy background of small coccobacilli, with few or no lactobacilli
Clue cells: squamous cells coated by coccobacilli that obscure the cell membrane

images.caption: Normal flora (lactobacilli, left) compared with bacterial vaginosis (coccobacilli coating a squamous cell, right) (Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Clue cells: squamous cells covered by coccobacilli that obscure the cell borders, in a filmy background (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Actinomyces
points: Tangled clumps of filamentous organisms (cotton balls), often with acute-angle branching and radiating filaments
Usually seen with an intrauterine device

images.caption: Actinomyces: a dense, tangled cotton-ball cluster of filamentous organisms with radiating filaments at its edge (Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Herpes simplex virus
points: Multinucleation, moulding and chromatin margination, giving ground-glass nuclei
Dense eosinophilic intranuclear (Cowdry A) inclusions in some cells

images.caption: Herpes simplex: multinucleation, nuclear moulding, chromatin margination and Cowdry A intranuclear inclusions (annotated, Pap stain).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Herpes simplex: multinucleated cells with moulded, ground-glass nuclei (ThinPrep).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Cytomegalovirus
points: Enlarged cells, usually endocervical, with a large eosinophilic intranuclear inclusion and a clear halo
Small granular cytoplasmic inclusions may be present

groups.heading: Reactive and reparative change
points: Inflammation: nuclei 1.5 to 2 times an intermediate nucleus, smooth outlines, fine chromatin; nucleoli and cytoplasmic halos may be present
Repair: flat cohesive sheets with streaming (school-of-fish) nuclei, distinct borders and prominent nucleoli; few single cells
Lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis: polymorphous lymphoid cells with tingible-body macrophages

groups.heading: Radiation and IUD effects
points: Radiation: marked cell enlargement without a raised N:C ratio; vacuolated or polychromatic cytoplasm, bi- and multinucleation, degenerate nuclei
IUD: small groups of vacuolated glandular cells (signet-ring forms) and single cells with a high N:C ratio that can mimic HSIL

images.caption: IUD-associated change: a small three-dimensional group of endometrial cells with cytoplasmic vacuolation and slightly enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, called AGC-NOS before the IUD was known (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 10

groups.heading: Atrophy
points: Flat sheets of parabasal cells with preserved polarity; nuclei may enlarge, with slight hyperchromasia
A granular basophilic background, blue blobs and inflammation are common

images.caption: Atrophy in a postmenopausal woman: a flat sheet of parabasal cells with evenly spaced nuclei and preserved polarity (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Alex_brollo, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Endometrial cells (45 or older)
points: Small, tight three-dimensional clusters; nuclei about the size of an intermediate nucleus, with scant cytoplasm and apoptotic debris
Reported in women aged 45 or older

images.caption: Exfoliated endometrial cells: a small, tight three-dimensional ball of cells with scant cytoplasm, beside a superficial squamous cell (Pap stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Endometrial cells in a woman over 40: a tight three-dimensional group of small cells with dark nuclei and scant cytoplasm (Pap stain).
images.credit: Keleş et al., Turk Patoloji Derg 2022, Fig 2

groups.heading: Keratotic change and tubal metaplasia
points: Hyperkeratosis: anucleate squames; parakeratosis: miniature superficial cells with dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and pyknotic nuclei
Tubal metaplasia: columnar cells with cilia and terminal bars; crowded, pseudostratified groups can mimic AIS

images.caption: Tubal metaplasia mimicking AIS, with milder crowding, elongation and stratification; no cilia were found and it was called AGC-NOS, endocervical (Pap stain, x400).
images.credit: Lai, Hsu and Li, IntechOpen 2012, Fig 12

groups.heading: Glandular cells post hysterectomy
points: Benign-appearing glandular cells in a vaginal vault sample after hysterectomy

fields.label: HPV test
options: Positive for other high-risk HPV types
Positive for HPV 16 and other high-risk types

fields.placeholder: e.g. Occasional groups of ciliated respiratory epithelial cells are also present

snippets.label: ASC-US: HPV triage

auto.is: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US)

snippets.text: Reflex high-risk HPV testing or repeat cytology in 6 to 12 months is advised according to the local screening guideline.

snippets.label: TZ absent: routine recall
snippets.text: The absence of a transformation zone component does not by itself warrant early repeat; routine recall is suggested.

snippets.label: Endometrial cells 45+: correlation
snippets.text: Benign-appearing endometrial cells in a woman aged 45 or older; clinical correlation with menstrual history and endometrial sampling as indicated is advised.

values.interpretation: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
